topics.question: How should a property comparison account for future flood exposure?

topics.question: Who can see the personal information attached to a property transaction?

topics.question: What changed for buyer-broker agreements and MLS compensation offers under the 2024 NAR settlement rules?
topics.coverage: Compare the dated NAR MLS practice changes with a sample buyer agreement; distinguish commission negotiability, who pays and actual transaction outcomes rather than assuming a mandatory six-percent rate or a uniform price effect.

topics.question: What conditions did Florida’s 2024 HB 621 set for removal of an unauthorized occupant?
topics.coverage: Read the enacted statute and an official procedure for a specific fact pattern; distinguish an unauthorized occupant from a tenant or title dispute, and do not imply a universal shortcut or offer individual legal advice.

topics.coverage: Use a dated IRS audit guide and a hypothetical property-component schedule to explain classification and documentation; separate depreciation timing from guaranteed savings and avoid individual tax advice.

topics.coverage: Use NYC Office of Special Enforcement rules and dated registration or enforcement records; distinguish compliance changes from evidence of host panic-selling or a national Airbnb market collapse.

# Real Estate Channel Master Topic Roadmap (Scratch to Advanced)
**Niche:** 112 Real Estate (Finance_Banking)  
**Channel Language:** English (YouTube)  
**Target Audience:** Property Investors, First-Time Homebuyers, Mortgage Brokers, Commercial Developers, RE Analysts (Global)  
**Production Format:** 10-Minute Documentary Explainer Episodes (600s, 75 Fixed 8s Scenes)

## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Real Estate across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Property Valuation, Cap Rates & Mortgage Mechanics (Beginner / Scratch)** — Discounted cash flow, Net Operating Income (NOI), Capitalization Rates (Cap Rates), 30-year fixed mortgages, amortization schedules, and title insurance.
- **Tier 2: Commercial Asset Classes, Syndications & Value-Add Playbooks (Intermediate)** — Multifamily vs industrial vs retail, real estate syndication waterfalls, BRRRR method (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat), 1031 tax-deferred exchanges, and lease structures (Triple Net / NNN).
- **Tier 3: Institutional Capital, REITs & Debt Securitization (Upper Intermediate)** — Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS), Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), mezzanine financing, debt-service coverage ratios (DSCR), and distressed asset workouts.
- **Tier 4: Macro Cycles, Demographic Shifts & Tokenized Property (Advanced / Masterclass)** — Homer Hoyt 18-year real estate cycle, demographic flight corridors, climate risk insurance insolvency, proptech fractionalization, and multi-billion development underwriting.

---

technical.requirements: Use the actual system documentation, a worked implementation and measurements. Identify inputs, outputs, constraints, tolerances, failure conditions and the limits of the example. Do not provide hazardous construction or unauthorized access procedures.
source_leads: official versioned product or standards documentation
test reports and drawings with clear provenance

finance.requirements: Use current official terms, filings or macroeconomic data; state jurisdiction, date, fees, taxes, risk, units and assumptions. Use transparent illustrative calculations rather than personal recommendations or return promises.
source_leads: actual contracts, fee schedules and audited filings
original economic studies and disclosed calculation inputs

civic.requirements: Use the current official legal text, policy, procedure or public dataset for a specific jurisdiction and date. Distinguish written rules, implementation and lived access; give no personal legal or financial conclusion.
source_leads: official laws, rules and administrative guidance
audits, judgments and public service records
consented accounts from affected people and qualified specialists

handoff: Keep the BANK ID in notes. Refine the research question with an exact text edition, jurisdiction, population, product version, place, time range or clearly labeled fictional premise.
Inspect actual sources; no source was verified by generating this map. Apply the existing registry planning and idea readiness process before project creation.
Choose a current registered angle only after reading its niche-specific scope. This initial map has not checked or assigned angle plans for these entries.
Keep Q1-Q42, CAT defaults, project snapshots, output locations and production gates unchanged. Catalog counts are not production or publication counts.
Review neighboring banks for semantic overlap and follow the existing Phase 1 claim-ledger requirements. Add qualified review when required by the production contract.
prior_initial_map.coverage_limits: This initial map does not exhaust the niche, its regions, time periods, named case studies, texts, technical variants or disputed questions. It has not performed source-feasibility checks, semantic duplicate review of every pair, trend analysis, claim verification or episode production. Expand any category freely after identifying a real coverage gap; add categories where the subject requires them. Preserve existing IDs when refining wording and allocate new IDs only for genuinely new proposals.

open_coverage.next_step: Select dated jurisdictions, editions, named sites, populations or product versions for the active proposals. Inspect actual sources before making factual claims; no research or production readiness was certified.
